commit_message:
winch: Simplify the handling of `wasm_load`s (#10012)

This commit aims to simplify how `wasm_load`s are currently handled in
the compiler by reducing the number of invariants that need to be
encoded at callsites which make their emission error prone.

Concretely this change:

* Augments `ExtendKind`, to account for unsigned extends; prior to this
  commit it wasn't explicit which loads required unsigned extends.
* Derive `OperandSize` from `ExtendKind`, removing from the caller the
  responsibility of encoding the operand size to use.

fix_commit_message: Winch: Fix Wasm vector loads to operate on 64-bits (#10127)
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix db7fb47b8e14 on top of intro bb5e4bbaf9a6 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): Wasmtime's Winch baseline (single-pass) compiler computes an `OperandSize` for each kind of Wasm load via `LoadKind::derive_operand_size()`. This size is used both to emit the machine-code load and, critically, to perform/encode the linear-memory bounds/guard check for the access. The January 2025 `wasm_load` simplification refactor (PR #10012) introduced `operand_size_for_vector()`, which derived a size of 1, 2, or 4 bytes for the SIMD 'vector extend' load variants (`v128.load8x8_{s,u}`, `v128.load16x4_{s,u}`, `v128.load32x2_{s,u}`) based on the *source lane width* rather than the *total bytes actually read*. All of these instructions read a full 8 bytes (64 bits) of linear memory and widen each lane, so the derived size undercounted the real access footprint by a factor of 2x-8x. PR #10127 fixed this by hard-coding `OperandSize::S64` for all `VectorExtendKind` variants. Root cause: The refactor in #10012 conflated 'bits per source lane before widening' with 'total bytes read from memory' when deriving the OperandSize for vector-extend loads. The derived size is reused for both bounds checking and instruction emission, so an incorrect (too-small) per-lane size was propagated into the memory-safety-relevant bounds computation instead of being independently fixed at 8 bytes (the true width of the SIMD extend-load instructions on x86-64/AArch64).
